title: Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization
abstract: For each positive Hölder exponent below one third, constructs a divergence-free periodic drift on the two-dimensional torus exhibiting anomalous dissipation for every mean-zero periodic H1 initial datum. The same drift admits uniform Hölder time estimates along a sequence of diffusivity intervals and two distinct vanishing-diffusivity limits for an explicit nonempty class of smooth data. Includes weak existence and uniqueness, Sobolev and Fourier/Galerkin infrastructure, flow derivatives, quantitative homogenization, and the multiscale construction. The no-selection result is the corrected version documented upstream, not the printed generality of the original paper's Proposition 5.5.

informal.AVenhance.anomalous_dissipation_full: For every alpha strictly between zero and one third, one periodic, divergence-free drift has joint spatial and temporal alpha-Hölder regularity and continuity into the spatial Hölder class. It exhibits anomalous dissipation with a positive rate depending only on the initial L2-to-gradient ratio, uniform Hölder-in-time L2 bounds along diffusivity intervals accumulating at zero, and two distinct transport limits along separated diffusivity sequences for a smooth mean-zero data class containing arbitrarily high cosine modes.
informal.AVenhance.anomalous_dissipation: For every positive alpha below one third there exists a periodic, divergence-free alpha-Hölder drift and a rate function taking values in (0,1], depending only on the initial L2-to-gradient ratio, such that the limsup as positive diffusivity tends to zero of integrated gradient dissipation is at least the squared rate times the initial L2 energy, for every mean-zero periodic H1 datum and corresponding weak solutions.
informal.AVenhance.weak_wellposed: Every bounded measurable periodic drift with positive diffusivity and periodic-cell L2 initial datum has a weak solution, unique up to spatial almost-everywhere equality at every time in [0,1].
